code: library(latents) set.seed(2026) n_teams <- 120 team_type <- rep(c("supportive", "strained"), times = c(66, 54)) team_size <- rep(c(4, 6, 8, 12), length.out = n_teams) team_climate <- rnorm(n_teams, ifelse(team_type == "supportive", 0.8, -0.8),                       ifelse(team_type == "supportive", 0.35, 0.6)) team_support <- rnorm(n_teams, ifelse(team_type == "supportive", 0.6, -0.5), 0.45) ratings <- data.frame(   team = rep(seq_len(n_teams), team_size),   type = rep(team_type, team_size),   climate = rep(team_climate, team_size) + rnorm(sum(team_size), 0, 0.9),   support = rep(team_support, team_size) + rnorm(sum(team_size), 0, 1)) str(ratings) #> 'data.frame':    900 obs. of  4 variables: #>  $ team   : int  1 1 1 1 2 2 2 2 2 2 ... #>  $ type   : chr  "supportive" "supportive" "supportive" "supportive" ... #>  $ climate: num  1.219 1.082 2.058 1.642 0.418 ... #>  $ support: num  -0.623 1.729 0.945 0.236 1.262 ...

title: Covariates, outcomes and staged estimation
text: Three-step methods assume classification errors independent external variable given true class, treat error matrix known. One-step coefficients conditional group class can change profiles, need equal three-step coefficients. Staged estimation carry first-stage uncertainty second stage, likelihood joint maximum. associations observational.

text: Information criteria compare candidates fitted, possible models. Classification measures describe fitted model; misspecified model can still classify sharply. Wald intervals assume converged fit variance bound, conditional chosen numbers profiles classes. Unmodelled dependence indicators can make extra classes look better.

title: Growth mixture models: classes of trajectories
text: Latent class growth analysis (Nagin 2005) gives every class trajectory. Everyone class follows trajectory exactly; anything else noise. also lets people vary around class trajectory: start rate change (random intercepts slopes). difference matters. people vary within kind, first model can express variation adding classes, tends find classes (Bauer Curran 2003). second model separates kinds change individual variation. one call. Persons classified units, id names class_level = "group" keeps person’s measurements one class; random adds random effects.

title: Growth mixture models: classes of trajectories
text: growth_scores simulated answer known: 300 students tested seven waves, three kinds (improving, stable, declining), student varying around kind’s trajectory, motivation predicting kind. 12% tests missed, models handle without imputation.

title: Multilevel latent profile analysis
text: Profiles means variances every group class. Observations independent given group’s class, groups independent one another. Indicators independent within profile (default diagonal covariance; covariance_model = "full" relaxes ). numbers profiles group classes chosen analyst; see evaluation vignette comparing .

title: Latent transition analysis
text: course_engagement one row per course enrolment: 1,422 enrolments 106 students. lta() needs three kinds variables. Group: student identifies whose occasions belong together. Occasion order: sequence position course student’s history. Students can different numbers occasions. Indicators: five activity measures (browse, lectures, forum_read, forum_post, attendance), standardized within course, 0 course average.
code: library(latents)

title: Latent transition analysis

title: Latent transition analysis
text: default assumption model can tested relaxing one argument: transition_covariates lets covariates shift transition probabilities: log odds moving profile rather staying. covariate may change occasions. initial_covariates lets covariates shift starting profile. transitions = "occasion" estimates separate transition matrix move. measurement = "occasion" lets profiles’ means variances differ occasion. order = 2 makes next profile depend two previous ones. mover_stayer = TRUE adds class groups never change profile. enumerate_classes(..., time = "sequence") compares numbers profiles group classes, bootstrap_lrt() tests model nested one. student’s grade previous course change likely move engagement profiles? previous_grade changes course course: grade’s odds ratios close one intervals include one: data, previous grade change chance switching profile. second-order chain, next profile depends two previous ones, earn extra parameters either: extensions return fit transition initial logit coefficients, Wald standard errors probabilities per occasion; checked Mplus, depmixS4 LMest.

text: mixture_regression() fits regressions whose coefficients differ across latent classes, continuous ("gaussian"), binary binomial ("binomial") count ("poisson") outcomes. class can belong row, whole group (class_level = "group"), row second-level group class shifts often regression class occurs within group (n_group_classes). code: set.seed(1) example_data <- data.frame(   school = rep(seq_len(10), each = 10),   score = rnorm(100, rep(c(-2, 2), each = 50)) ) smaller <- multilpa(example_data, "score", "school", n_profiles = 1,                     n_group_classes = 1, n_starts = 2, seed = 1) larger <- multilpa(example_data, "score", "school", n_profiles = 2,                    n_group_classes = 1, n_starts = 2, seed = 1) # `iter` is small so the example runs quickly; use many more for inference. comparison <- bootstrap_lrt(smaller, larger, iter = 9, n_starts = 1,                             max_iter = 2000, tol = 1e-6, seed = 1) comparison #> Parametric bootstrap likelihood-ratio comparison #> Null: 1 profile; alternative: 2 profiles #> Observed statistic: 44.198110 #> p-value: 0.1 (Monte Carlo SE 0.0949) from 9 of 9 valid replicates

what: Reading growth of students nested in schools — growth_schools
title: Reading growth of students nested in schools — growth_schools
text: simulated multilevel longitudinal dataset made multilevel growth mixture model. 600 students 40 schools (15 per school) sit reading test five occasions (wave 0 4). Two kinds student follow two trajectories: improving (starts near 48, gains 3 points wave) plateauing (starts near 56, gains 0.3). Students vary around trajectory (random intercept SD 3, random slope SD 0.6, correlation -0.2; residual SD 2). Schools two types: supportive schools 80% students improve, struggling schools 25% , school's support programme (standardized, measured ) makes likely supportive. 8% tests missed random.

title: Achievement growth of students with three kinds of trajectory — growth_scores
text: simulated longitudinal dataset made growth models. 300 students sit achievement test seven occasions (wave 0 6). Three kinds student follow three trajectories: improving (starts near 48, gains 3.5 points wave), stable (starts near 62, gains 0.5) declining (starts near 58, loses 2.5). Within kind, students vary around trajectory: start rate change (random intercept SD 4, random slope SD 0.8, correlation -0.3, spread every kind), residual SD 3. Motivation, measured , makes student likely improving less likely declining. 12% tests missed random, panel unbalanced.

title: Study hours and quiz scores under two study strategies — study_hours
text: 150 students report six study weeks. every week student studies one two strategies, strategy decides hours become quiz score: deep week gains 4.5 points per hour base 35, surface week one point per hour base 55. Students two kinds differ mix strategies – steady students study deeply 85% weeks, erratic ones 25% – higher motivation makes student likely steady. sleep makes deep week likely. score ~ hours two-class mixture level week (class_level = "observation"), whose class shares differ student (two-level model, id = "student", n_group_classes = 2). passed depends student's kind, week's strategy, mixture level student (class_level = "group"). questions count whose Poisson regression depends week's strategy.

title: Relate a latent class to an outcome it did not help define — three_step
code: set.seed(11) group <- rep(seq_len(40), each = 10) truth <- 1L + as.integer(runif(400) > 0.5) example_data <- data.frame(   g = group,   a = rnorm(400, ifelse(truth == 2L, 1.1, -1.1)),   b = rnorm(400, ifelse(truth == 2L, 1.1, -1.1)),   y = rnorm(400, ifelse(truth == 2L, 10, 0)) ) fit <- multilpa(example_data, c("a", "b"), "g", n_profiles = 2,                 n_group_classes = 1, n_starts = 4, seed = 1) three_step(fit, example_data, "y") #> Distal outcome by class (bch, 95% CI) #>  #> Class    Mean            95% CI    SE  Effective n #> -----  ------  ----------------  ----  ----------- #>     1  -0.069  [-0.458,  0.321]  0.20       182.75 #>     2   9.972  [ 9.537, 10.407]  0.22       170.37 three_step(fit, example_data, "y", contrast = "pairs") #> Distal outcome: class differences (bch, 95% CI) #>  #> Class  vs  Difference         95% CI      p  p (BH) #> -----  --  ----------  -------------  -----  ------ #>     2   1       10.04  [9.37, 10.71]  <.001   <.001
